prompt:
Image 1 is a flat lay of a Ice Hockey kit, photographed from the front.

Photograph THAT SAME KIT from the BACK — the same garments, turned over:
- the shirt, laid flat and face DOWN, so its back is what you see
- the shorts below it, also turned so their back is what you see
EXACTLY ONE of each. No socks, no shoes, no ball, nothing else in the frame.

Everything carries over from image 1 unchanged: the same colours, the same fabric, the
same cut, the same collar, and above all the SAME PANELS AND
TRIM — a stripe, a panel or a piping that exists on the front continues around to the
back exactly as the garment's construction would carry it. Nothing is added that image 1
does not have, and nothing that image 1 has quietly disappears.

SLEEVES: this is the same garment as image 1, so it has exactly the same sleeves. If the
shirt in image 1 has short sleeves, this one has short sleeves and is NOT a sleeveless
vest or a tank top. If image 1 is sleeveless, this one is sleeveless. Look at image 1 and
copy what is there.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: NAVY ice hockey jersey, loose and squared off the way a hockey sweater is, with a laced V-neck collar. The trim is RED and there is exactly this much of it: a red edge to the collar, one wide red band around the waist hem, and one red band around each sleeve at the forearm. The club crest sits LARGE and CENTRED on the chest. The number 17 appears on BOTH SHOULDERS in white, and large across the upper back. There is NO number on the front, no player name, no club name, no sponsor and no lettering of any kind. Solid navy everywhere else — no contrast shoulders, no contrast sleeve panels, no piping.
- shorts: Navy ice hockey breezers (padded pants) to just below the knee, matte navy with subtle darker navy panels and no trim. PLAIN AND UNBRANDED: no manufacturer's wordmark on the thigh or anywhere else.
- socks: Navy knit hockey socks pulled up over the knee pads to mid-thigh, plain, no stripes and no logo.
- footwear: Black ice hockey SKATES with white laces, a stiff moulded boot, a silver-grey blade holder and a steel blade. Never trainers, never boots. PLAIN AND UNBRANDED: no swoosh, no wordmark, no maker's mark.
- equipment: A NAVY ice hockey helmet with a CLEAR FLAT VISOR over the eyes — a visor, never a full cage and never a grille, because the face has to be readable — with a white chin cup and black straps. Navy gloves with red trim at the cuff. A plain black rubber puck. A plain wood-toned stick with black tape on the blade. THE HELMET SHELL IS PLAIN: no maker's mark, no decal, no sticker, no warning label, no lettering anywhere on it. The same helmet, gloves, stick and puck in every shot.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits LARGE and CENTRED on the chest, filling the middle of the jersey between the collar and the waist band, about two hand-widths across — the way a hockey club's crest always sits. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

THE BACK OF THE SHIRT carries the squad number 17, plus whatever else the
kit description above explicitly gives it — and nothing more. Add no mark the description
does not name.
NEVER any lettering: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no word of any kind.
Nothing sits inside, on top of or overlapping the numerals — a badge, if the description
calls for one, is small, clear of the number, and the right way round.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no wear, no sweat marks.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- The same plain light grey surface and the same even lighting as image 1.
- No text of any kind beyond the number, no labels, no neck tag, no watermark.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
